name: Workforce diversity, equity and inclusion programmes
one_line: The employer-side record of measuring and acting on the composition and inclusiveness of its OWN workforce: protected-characteristic self-declaration instruments, monitoring exports, statutory equality returns and pay-gap disclosures, equality/affirmative-action plans, pay-equity and adverse-impact analyses, employee network and sponsorship programmes, and progress reporting against stated objectives. It is not established by the words diversity, equity or inclusion, by a DEI-titled training certificate, or by an external sustainability report; activation requires a workforce population or a self-declaration instrument joined to a monitoring, reporting or programme structure. PLACEHOLDER row on the fieldless hr schema (PR-6): fields stay empty and every characteristic value is treated as protected before any cloud step.

deterministic: a workforce data export whose header row JOINTLY names an organisational population (business unit, site, grade, job group, level) and at least one protected-characteristic column (ethnicity, race, gender identity, disability status, veteran status, religion, sexual orientation) together with a monitoring measure (headcount, share, representation, promotion rate, attrition). The joint header structure is the signal; a characteristic column alone is a survey or census artefact, and a population column alone is ordinary workforce analytics

a statutory equality return whose page-one or sheet labels match a named reporting instrument's fixed structure: job-category rows crossed by race/ethnicity and sex counts beside an establishment or employer identifier and a filing period; or mean and median hourly pay gap and bonus gap figures beside a pay-quartile distribution and a signed accuracy statement

a self-declaration instrument carrying a protected-characteristic question set beside an explicit non-response option (prefer not to say, I do not wish to answer, decline to state) and a voluntariness or lawful-basis paragraph. The non-response option is the discriminating slot: it distinguishes an employer monitoring instrument from a demographic field on an ordinary personnel form

an equality or affirmative-action plan whose labelled sections combine job groups, an availability analysis, an incumbency-versus-availability comparison, and placement or representation goals with a plan period

a pay or selection analysis whose columns pair a remuneration figure or a stage-by-stage outcome count with a group flag and a computed per-group ratio, gap or regression residual, plus a model or methodology tab

a workforce network or cohort programme record whose labelled slots combine a named employee network or targeted cohort, an executive sponsor, eligibility criteria, objectives, and a budget or activity plan explicitly scoped to the organisation's own employees
a governance progress report whose tables restate the organisation's own representation against previously stated objectives with named baselines, reporting periods, and an owner per objective
needs_llm: whether a demographic cut describes the organisation's OWN workforce or is a benchmark, market-research or peer dataset about other employers. Identical column shapes occur in both; only the population statement, employee identifiers or an internal system header settle it
whether a document is the governing equality or equal-opportunities policy, which is a business_operations record, or programme delivery and monitoring carried out under it, which is this row

whether protected-characteristic data describes employees or job APPLICANTS. Applicant-stage monitoring is a recruiting corpus; this row holds it only when the artefact is the employer's aggregate monitoring or statutory reporting instrument

whether a low-count cell is a deliberate suppression artefact or an unsuppressed re-identifying figure. Aggregation is not proof of safety here; the safe response is to protect, keep the judgement local, and abstain rather than summarise the cells

whether an inclusion or belonging measure is a demographic cut of one engagement wave, whose instrument and response file belong to the engagement-survey sibling, or a standalone monitoring instrument fielded for this programme
whether a heterogeneous packet is purpose-coherent as one reporting obligation when its members include a data extract, an analysis workbook, legal advice, a narrative draft, and a signed return
never_alone: the words diversity, equity, inclusion, DEI, EDI, belonging, equality, representation, or bias alone. They appear in recruitment marketing, ESG and sustainability reports, vendor pitch decks, job adverts, university syllabi, and academic articles

protected-characteristic vocabulary alone: ethnicity, race, gender, disability, veteran, religion and sexual orientation appear in census extracts, clinical letters, immigration forms, customer market research, and survey instruments that are not about a workforce

a completion certificate, roster row, or calendar invite for a DEI-titled training course. The topic of a course is a value of a work type, not a filing world; a training completion record is a learning record whatever its subject

one individual's own self-declaration or adjustment record held in a personal corpus. That is the individual's identity, health or employment record; the employer-side monitoring reading requires a workforce population or an employer instrument
an external sustainability, ESG, annual-report or careers-site section about people, however many representation figures it prints. Its audience is external and it carries no workforce rows
the employer's own name, letterhead, email domain, or a parent directory named DEI, EDI, People, Inclusion, or Confidential
a percentage, gap figure, ratio, index score, base size, bare year, or acronym such as EEO, AAP, GPG, ERG, MBE
a supplier, contractor or vendor certification of diverse ownership. That describes a supply base, not a workforce, and belongs with sourcing evidence
source type or extension alone, including spreadsheet, email, calendar, PDF, image, OCR, archive, or contacts
absence of EXIF as proof that an image of a diversity dashboard, self-ID portal, or monitoring return is a screenshot
membership in a download session, mailbox folder, or shared-drive folder

work_types: workforce diversity monitoring export or representation report
statutory equality return or published pay-gap disclosure
voluntary self-identification instrument, declaration record, or declaration-rate report
equality or affirmative-action plan with availability, utilisation and goal analysis
pay equity audit or remuneration-gap analysis and its methodology
inclusion, belonging or fairness measure derived from an employee listening instrument
employee resource group charter, membership record, budget request, or activity plan
mentoring, sponsorship, or targeted development cohort record
accessibility and workplace-adjustment programme standard or monitoring record
DEI strategy, objective set, or board and executive progress report
grouping_reasons: one reporting obligation instance: a snapshot or reference date with its data extract, analysis workbook, narrative draft, review advice, sign-off and filed or published return
one monitoring wave: an instrument, its response or declaration file, the declaration-rate report, and the resulting representation analysis
one named programme: a network or cohort across charter, eligibility, budget, calendar, membership record and activity report
one plan period: an equality or affirmative-action plan with its job-group analyses, goals, and progress updates
sparse members such as a one-page approval, a suppression note, or a chart image may join an accepted group by membership without copying a population, characteristic, period or gap figure onto them
one duplicate or version family through universal duplicate_family and version_family facts, not through a DEI-only field

no group is valid when a lone DEI-worded file lacks a workforce population, a self-declaration instrument, or a reporting structure. Protected residual placement is safer than inventing an employer monitoring corpus

template.why: Empty by PR-6: the hr schema declares no canonical field rows, so no proposed key may become a folder dimension here. The recommendation is held as prose for R1c and differs deliberately from the hr default. The hr default leads with work type or a named people programme, then workforce unit or cohort, then people cycle. This row inverts and truncates that: lead with the reporting or programme instance (the obligation or the named network), then work type, and treat workforce unit as NOT visible by default, because a folder tree branching on business unit or site publishes the composition of small populations at exactly the granularity that re-identifies individuals. An employee name level is forbidden outright, since the branch label would itself disclose a declared characteristic. It is not time-first: a snapshot date qualifies a reporting obligation and is not the world's organising fact; two files bearing the same year may belong to unrelated obligations.

observations: fixed job-category rows (executive and senior officials, professionals, technicians, craft workers, laborers) crossed by race and ethnicity columns and by sex
establishment identifier, employer identification block, and a reporting-period label
a certification page with a signatory and submission timestamp
must_not_conclude: any hr fact as canonical, because this placeholder schema declares no fields
that a submitted return proves the underlying counts are correct, complete, or currently accurate
that a filed return is low sensitivity because filing is compulsory
a folder path

sensitivity_why: The evidence set is built out of protected or special-category characteristics declared by identifiable individuals, and the aggregate artefacts do not neutralise that. A representation table cut by unit, grade and characteristic re-identifies people whenever a cell is small, and suppressed cells are frequently reconstructable from margins, so aggregation must not be read as anonymisation. Declaration instruments additionally carry a voluntariness and separate-holding expectation that joining them to the payroll or personnel corpus would defeat. The row therefore defaults to local-only handling and abstention rather than remote summarisation. This is the only sensitivity value available in this phase; P7 owns handling classes and no class is asserted here.
open_question: Whether the statutory-return leg (EEO-1, pay-gap disclosure, affirmative-action plan) belongs to this row or to business_operations.corporate-regulatory-filings, and whether this row survives R1c as distinct from hr.workforce-analytics once the demographic-cut fixture is adjudicated. See NJ-DEI-1 through NJ-DEI-5 in the research memo.
